text: We're closing out chapter two with NULL handling -- and one surprise specific to a single platform that trips up even experienced developers.

Start with what's actually consistent everywhere: equals null never matches, on every single platform in this course. Middle name equals null will never find a row, no matter which database you're on. You always need is null, or is not null, instead.

On SQL Server, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, insert an empty string into a column, and it stays an empty string. Check it with is null, and it won't match. Check it with equals empty string, and it will. Empty string and null are two genuinely different things.

Oracle breaks that pattern completely. Insert that same empty string into a varchar2 column, and Oracle quietly stores it as null instead. Check it with is null, and it matches. Check it with equals empty string, and nothing ever matches, because equals null never matches anything, anywhere.

Here's why it catches people off guard: code that distinguishes "no value given" from "a blank value was given" -- a totally normal pattern for optional text fields -- silently loses that distinction the moment it runs against Oracle. There's no error. The empty string just quietly becomes null.

That wraps up chapter two on data types. Chapter three moves to querying basics compared, starting with pagination -- top, rownum and fetch first, and limit -- going much deeper than the quick preview we saw back in lesson five. See you there.
